gen-archivo-black-fs-bespoke-serif: Bespoke Serif carries a dignified text serif voice, its thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones. But Archivo Black stays heavy and low-contrast, so making it small would squeeze that urban punch into a smudge.
gen-archivo-black-fs-sentient: Archivo Black fills the middle of every line with a big, blunt lowercase. Sentient is the foil, pinched and a touch crayon-rough, with a moderate height that makes the headline look even heavier.
gen-boska-bitter: Boska has stems like carved stone and serifs that look scratched into glass, which gives it real drama. Bitter follows with a very large lowercase eye and gaps in each s you can see through, so a slightly generous body size feels natural.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-zcool-xiaowei: ZCOOL XiaoWei has rounded letters that thicken slightly at their sides, and its weight shifts gently from stem to serif. Yet Oswald does the tightly knit, confident job better up top, while the body font handles the quiet, modern reading.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-zen-kaku-gothi: Marker-bold and full of daylight in every curve. Zen Kaku Gothic Antique takes the quieter job, with a t whose crossbar matches its stem and curves that glide smoothly, while Red Hat Display does the loud talking.
gen-gf-unica-one-gf-sarpanch: Sarpanch reads like a plain sans with a clearly open e and a compact gap between x-height and ascender line. And Unica One, with its tubelike lines and huge lowercase, would sit above that text with confidence over a longer stretch.
gen-gf-wallpoet-gf-savate: Savate reads with sturdy hairlines and open jaws on every curve, its rounded o nearly matching the capital. And Wallpoet stays the bold, high-rising headline, so enlarging the body a notch lets those tall shapes breathe.
gen-irish-grover-gf-sofia-sans: Playful is the first word for Irish Grover, whose tall lowercase makes words look sturdy and large. Sofia Sans runs beneath it as a plain sans with no thick-thin modulation, so the soft, organic top meets a line like spaghetti.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-stack-sans-headline: Luckiest Guy shouts with a high mean line and ink that looks poured. Stack Sans Headline works under it with wide gaps, a deep middle band and a monoline skeleton, giving the loud top a sturdy, approachable partner.
gen-megrim-gf-sono: Futuristic and angular, Megrim ends every stroke at one measured thickness. Sono, a plain sans with tall lowercase and an ajar mouth on each a, spreads out with wide spacing, so a longer read feels unhurried.
